transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-12
Time: 15:00 UTC (48 minutes)
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE); Samir Rao (Redwood SE); Lena Ortiz (Redwood Marketing) — Alicia Chen (BrightWave CTO); Marco Ruiz (BrightWave Head of ML); Jasmine Lee (BrightWave Product Marketing)

[00:00] Maya Patel: Hi everyone, welcome, thanks for making time. This is Maya from Redwood Inference, with Samir our SE and Lena from marketing. How's everyone doing?
[00:06] Alicia Chen: Good, thanks. Excited for this, thanks for coordinating.
[00:09] Marco Ruiz: Yeah thanks, ready to chat.
[00:11] Jasmine Lee: Hi all, hello.
[00:15] Lena Ortiz: Quick note — we'll record this for the podcast and we will send over the recording and the transcript, if there's anything you'd like redacted just tell us.
[00:22] Alicia Chen: Sounds good.
[00:24] Maya Patel: Awesome. For structure, we'll start with a bit of background, then the technical story — Samir will ask a few questions — then we do marketing-y questions for quotes and outcomes. Does that work?
[00:31] Marco Ruiz: Works for me.

[02:00] Maya Patel: Alicia, can you give a brief background on BrightWave and what problem you're solving?
[02:06] Alicia Chen: Sure. BrightWave's a customer experience automation company, we help retailers personalize email and on-site messaging at scale. Historically we've used smaller models for scoring but we wanted better natural language understanding for our product descriptions and to generate tailored subject lines at scale.
[02:25] Maya Patel: And when did Redwood first come into the picture?
[02:29] Alicia Chen: We started a pilot in early 2025, around Feb–March, primarily to test inference latency and cost on live traffic. We'd been running a hybrid self-hosted approach and also trying managed endpoints from a few providers but latency and cost were both problems; we had cold-start issues and unpredictability in throughput.

[04:10] Samir Rao: Quick clarifying question: when you say unpredictability, was that due to autoscaling lag, underlying infra, or model selection?
[04:18] Marco Ruiz: It was a mix. Autoscaling on our prior provider would take minutes for heavier sequences, and our on-prem setup struggled with throughput under burst traffic. We needed better routing and more predictable batching. Redwood's dedicated option was attractive because of the reserved capacity.

[06:00] Samir Rao: Can you describe the integration? Was it a one-week POC or longer? Any custom infra?
[06:07] Marco Ruiz: POC took about four weeks. We did a canary on 10% traffic, validated latency SLOs, then ramped. We used Redwood's SDK and the vpc private endpoint — some of our network team had to configure private subnets and SAML SSO for dev access. There was a short hiccup with our KMS policies but that was resolved.
[06:36] Maya Patel: Thank you. On the model side, what are you running — off-the-shelf open models or fine-tuned variants?
[06:43] Alicia Chen: We used a fine-tuned Llama derivative for generation and a smaller embedding model for similarity. The fine-tuned model had an instruction-tuned head for marketing-style outputs. We also experimented with quantized variants for cost savings.

[08:30] Jasmine Lee: From a product standpoint, the biggest win was more relevant subject lines and fewer manual QA cycles. The content looked more on-brand after fine-tuning and the rollout to customers increased open rates 8–10 percent in initial A/Bs.

[10:00] Maya Patel: Nice. Marco, can you share some numbers on latency and cost after moving to Redwood?
[10:06] Marco Ruiz: Sure — p50 latency for our typical 64-token generation is down from ~220ms to ~95ms when routed to dedicated capacity. Costs per 1k tokens decreased roughly 30% after adjusting batching and using a 4-bit quantized model in non-critical paths. Real-world throughput improved because of smarter batching and prefix/KV cache reuse.

[12:40] Samir Rao: There was mention of prefix/KV cache — did you change your application to benefit or was it automatic?
[12:46] Marco Ruiz: Mostly automatic. We did tune prompt shapes a bit to increase cache hits, but Redwood's runtime handles KV cache intelligently so repeated context was reused. That was a big ops win.

[15:00] Maya Patel: Were there security or compliance requirements that required the private deployment?
[15:06] Alicia Chen: We handle PII in some pipelines and some enterprise customers demanded data residency controls and audit logs. So the Private option with VPC and customer-managed KMS was essential. We also needed SOC 2 and ISO references for our procurement team.
[15:28] Maya Patel: Thanks — we shared the SOC 2 and compliance pack earlier (link: https://redwood.example.com/security-pack), we'll re-send.

[17:00] Marco Ruiz: There was one incident during ramp where we hit an unexpected token rate flat — turned out a downstream job spiked and caused request bursts. Redwood's fallback routing to hosted capacity avoided impacting latency for customer-facing traffic, so UX stayed stable.
[17:28] Maya Patel: Good to hear fallbacks helped. Any surprises during deployment?
[17:34] Alicia Chen: The biggest surprise was how much our cost model improved once we tuned batching and used caching. Also, the ease of running A/Bs with Redwood Console dashboards made the product team much more confident.

[20:00] Jasmine Lee: From marketing, we loved the trace dashboards — we pulled token-level cost breakdowns for specific routes to justify the investment to finance.

[22:00] Lena Ortiz: Can we get a short quote from Alicia on outcome and from Marco on technical impact for the case study? Maybe one sentence each.
[22:10] Lena Ortiz: Example: "Redwood cut our inference latency in half and reduced per-token cost, enabling feature rollout at scale." Would that be OK?
[22:18] Alicia Chen: That's close — maybe: "Redwood halved our p50 latency and reduced per-token cost by ~30%, which let us ship personalized campaigns without compromising throughput."
[22:30] Marco Ruiz: For me: "Dedicated capacity and KV caching gave us predictable latency under burst traffic, simplifying our operational runbook."

[24:00] Maya Patel: Great — we'll capture those and send them over. Quick note on approval flow for the case study: we'll send a draft, Jasmine will review, legal signs off. Timeline target early January.

[26:00] Alicia Chen: Sounds good. A few product-specific questions — Samir, what tips would you recommend for reducing hallucinations in marketing copy generation?
[26:08] Samir Rao: We recommend prompt engineering with stronger constraints, using retrieval augmentation for factual pieces, and conservative decoding (lower temperature) for high-precision outputs. Also run small evals against a holdout prompt set — Redwood Optimize has tooling for that.
[26:34] Marco Ruiz: We also run a reranker stage using embeddings so low-certainty outputs are filtered out or rephrased.

[29:00] Lena Ortiz: For the podcast, any anecdotes about an early customer reaction?
[29:06] Alicia Chen: One of our pilot customers noted that subject lines felt "more human" and open rates jumped, but they also flagged a case where the model invented a promo code, which we caught with a filter. That led us to add a simple sanitization step.

[31:00] Maya Patel: Nice anecdote. Do you have any metrics on revenue impact?
[31:06] Jasmine Lee: Early signals — the 8–10% open rate improvement translated to a 3% uplift in conversion in initial segments, but it's early. We're tracking downstream LTV impact.

[33:30] Samir Rao: On the operations side, how has the team handled rollouts and model versioning?
[33:36] Marco Ruiz: We use Redwood's rollout features — canary at 10%, then 50% then full. Version pinning and automatic fallback made it safe to test new fine-tunes. We keep a shadow traffic stream for monitoring.

[36:00] Lena Ortiz: Marketing question — Jasmine, would you be open to a short video testimonial later?
[36:05] Jasmine Lee: Yeah, potentially. Need to check with legal but happy to consider.

[38:00] Maya Patel: Thanks everyone. Any final clarifications?
[38:05] Alicia Chen: Could you send the security pack and the one-pager on pricing tiers?
[38:10] Maya Patel: Absolutely — I'll send both today.

[40:00] Marco Ruiz: One tech note: we found the console's trace search invaluable for digging into token-level regressions; that saved us a week during a noisy rollout.
[40:10] Samir Rao: Glad that helped.

[42:00] Lena Ortiz: We'll plan to share the edited audio + transcript by 2025-12-20. Also we'll draft a 1-pager case study and send to Jasmine for quotes.

[44:00] Jasmine Lee: Thanks, we'll aim to review by 2025-12-22.

[46:00] Maya Patel: Recap of next steps: Lena will send audio and transcript; Maya will reshare the security/compliance pack and pricing one-pager; Jasmine will review quotes; legal will review logo/case language. Any other items?
[46:18] Alicia Chen: No, that's it. Thanks for hosting.
[46:22] Maya Patel: Thanks all — we'll follow up.
[46:25] [Recording stopped]
